questions.analogue: Why does continuity of f_h follow from f in L^p: which hypotheses does the primitive argument consume, and in what order?
questions.merge_note: The dialogue question asked which lemma a mislabelled citation denoted; the mathematical content is the two-stage route (integrability, then the primitive lemma), which is what is carried forward.

teaching.reason: The two stages, L^p inside L^1 and then the primitive, are the spine of the continuity half for a student.

expert-reference.reason: The expert needs only the primitive lemma; the L^p ⊂ L^1 step is automatic at this level.

formal-audit.reason: The audit lane should expose the finite-measure instance behind integrability and the NoAtoms instance behind the primitive lemma.

questions.analogue: Why estimate the symmetric difference of two windows at all, rather than writing the moving integral as a difference of two continuous primitives?
questions.merge_note: The informal solution's symmetric-difference measure should read 2 min(|s-t|, 2h), not 2|s-t|: the identity fails once |s-t| exceeds 2h, where the windows are disjoint and the measure is 4h. Clipping at the ends of [0,1] only shrinks the difference. The primitive route recorded as node B4 avoids the case split and the p = 1 fallback to absolute continuity; the dialogue thread ask-1795503347-388 is the evidence.

teaching.reason: The student should see why the primitive is the better object: one argument for all p, no exponent bookkeeping, no p = 1 exception.

expert-reference.reason: Either route is one line for an expert; the reference proof simply takes the primitive one.

formal-audit.reason: The Lean proof's own comment says the primitive route avoids symmetric-difference bookkeeping; the audit lane should record that choice.

questions.analogue: Is the restriction t ∈ [0,1] needed in the bound, or does the same estimate hold for every real t?
questions.merge_note: The warrant consumes only measurability, the window-measure bound (which holds for every t), and the exponent condition; it does not consume t ∈ [0,1], so the result extends to all real t.

teaching.reason: Noticing which hypotheses a proof never uses is a habit worth teaching, and here it widens the statement for free.

expert-reference.reason: The reference states the theorem as asked; the strengthening is a remark an expert supplies mentally.

formal-audit.reason: In the Lean proof the t ∈ [0,1] binder is introduced and never used in the bound branch; the audit lane should record that.

questions.analogue: Why is (2h)^(-1/p) the right constant in the bound?
questions.merge_note: Nobody asked this in the dialogue, but the blueprint needs it: the constant is the L^q norm of the normalised window indicator, (2h)^(-1) times (2h)^(1/q), including q = ∞ when p = 1.

teaching.reason: The constant looks arbitrary until it is recognised as a dual norm; that recognition is the teaching payload.

expert-reference.reason: An expert reads the constant as the dual norm of the box kernel without help.

formal-audit.reason: The Lean proof reaches the constant by exponent arithmetic on Hölder's (2h)^(1-1/p) followed by division by 2h; the audit lane should show both computations agree.
